Predicates:
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are the good guys.
Win(x) ::: x wins.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: x is the nemesis of y.
NamedAfter(y, x) ::: y is named after x.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
InMovie(x, y) ::: x is in movie y.
Movie(y) ::: y is a movie.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Wings(x, y) ::: x wins y.

Premises:
∀x (GoodGuys(x) → Win(x)) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(theMovie) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
Fight(SirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
NamedAfter(theMovie, SirDigby) ::: The movie is named after Sir Digby.
Character(SirDigby) ::: Sir Digby is a character.
InMovie(SirDigby, theMovie) ::: Sir Digby is in the movie.
InMovie(nemesis, theMovie) ::: The nemesis is in the movie.
Fight(x, y) → ¬Win(y) ::: If someone wins a fight, their opponent does not win.
NamedAfter(y, x) → Character(x) ::: If a movie is named after a character, that character is a character.
NamedAfter(y, x) → InMovie(x, y) ::: If a movie is named after a character, the character is in the movie.

Conclusion:
¬Win(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby's nemesis does not win.
